problem: Existing VLN agents suffer from spurious associations from dataset bias and confounders in vision and language, giving a large seen/unseen performance gap. Prior data augmentation does not remove these biases, and prior causal methods intervene only at the output layer with a fixed confounder dictionary.
motivation: Data scarcity and dataset bias (e.g. P(door|photo)=80% in R2R, dropping to 62% under do-intervention) hurt generalization to unseen environments. Intervening on the input-to-feature link, with a dictionary that tracks the changing network weights, should give unbiased representations that generalize better.
key_idea: Apply backdoor adjustment between inputs and intermediate features, using confounder dictionaries (objects, room types, direction/landmark words) that are updated iteratively during training, to learn unbiased visual and linguistic features for a DUET/DSRG-style navigator.
insight: Intervening at the feature level with an iteratively updated confounder dictionary improves unseen-environment generalization. In the R2R ablations, Best+Schedule updating (SR 74.07, SPL 64.34) beats a fixed pre-computed dictionary (72.92/63.42) and random initialization (72.24/63.14). All three confounder types together are best (#8: SR 74.07 vs baseline 71.65). Attention-based intervention suits language, which is trained end-to-end, while the statistic-based one suits vision, whose features are frozen and pre-extracted.
method: Structural causal model: a graph over inputs V and T, confounders Z_V and Z_T, features F_V, F_T, F_X and action A; the goal is the true link input→feature, deconfounded by backdoor adjustment.

IBRL module: models E_z[f(x,z)] = g(x)+E_z[q(z)] over a confounder dictionary. Type-1 (statistic) uses a prior-weighted sum of dictionary entries; Type-2 (attention) uses x as query and the dictionary as key/value.

Iterative dictionary update: the dictionary is initialized from average features per confounder class and re-computed with the current encoder when the loss improves (Best) or every 3K iterations (Schedule). It is applied in the language branch, where BERT trains end-to-end.

Visual backdoor causal encoder: object dictionary (43 classes, bottom-up attention features) and room-type dictionary (top 50 from BLIP VQA prompts, CLIP features). Image and object branches are 2-layer self-attention encoders with IBRL, then cross-attention with images as queries.

Linguistic backdoor causal encoder: 9-layer BERT. NLTK extracts direction and landmark words to build two dictionaries. IBRL is applied to each, the outputs are summed, and a sigmoid gate mixes them with the original features.
Memory-augmented global-local fusion (from DSRG): global adaptive aggregation, recurrent memory, LXMERT cross-modal encoders, and DUET-style dynamic global/local action fusion.
Training: pre-training with MLM+SAP (+OG for REVERIE), then fine-tuning with teacher forcing and PID sampling. Optional speaker augmentation: PASTS on R2R, RES-StS on REVERIE, Marky-mT5 on RxR.

setting.backbone: CLIP-ViT-B image features + bottom-up attention object features + 9-layer BERT + 2-layer vision encoders + 4-layer LXMERT cross-modal encoder (DUET/DSRG-style topological planner), trained end-to-end
setting.training_data: R2R / RxR-English / REVERIE training sets with pre-training (MLM, SAP, OG); optional speaker-generated augmentation (PASTS for R2R, RES-StS for REVERIE, Marky-mT5 for RxR)
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views) with CLIP features, bottom-up object features, heading/elevation orientation
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (global topological map candidates)
setting.privileged: none at test time (BLIP room labels and object detector are used only to build the training dictionary)

numbers_note: R2R values are printed as integers in the main table; the ablation table gives finer values (e.g. 74.07/64.34 on R2R val-unseen).
results: CausalVLN reaches R2R val-unseen SR 74 / SPL 64 (76/67 with PASTS), beating DSRG (73/62) and DUET (72/60). On REVERIE val-unseen it gets SR 50.44 / RGS 34.82 versus DSRG 47.83 / 32.69, though SPL and RGSPL drop. On RxR-English val-unseen it reaches SR 62.0 / sDTW 49.4 versus MARVAL 50.2 / 43.9.
limitations: Seen-environment R2R performance drops slightly, and SPL / RGSPL fall on REVERIE unseen (the agent explores more).

The confounders are hand-assumed (objects, rooms, direction/landmark words) and depend on external tools (BLIP, NLTK, object detector). The visual side is not updated iteratively because the extractors are frozen.
Weak sensitivity to numerical descriptions, shown in a failure case (stops in the first dining room instead of the second).
